builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation
summary: The method replaces standard knowledge distillation during an early phase of pretraining by training the student to match the teacher on perturbed inputs (additive token noise, blended documents, or blended tokens) before reverting to ordinary distillation for the remaining token budget. It costs additional teacher forward passes on perturbed sequences and requires access to both teacher logits and pretraining compute from scratch. The gains can fail to transfer if the reader lacks pretraining infrastructure, relies on third-party APIs that do not expose logits, or operates at scales or data regimes where the reported small-margin improvements vanish.
rationale: The technique targets pretraining from scratch with full access to teacher internals, which exceeds the reader's constrained infrastructure of one 24 GB GPU and third-party APIs.

claims.statement: The method replaces standard knowledge distillation during an early phase of pretraining by training the student to match the teacher on perturbed inputs (additive token noise, blended documents, or blended tokens) before reverting to ordinary distillation for the remaining token budget. It costs additional teacher forward passes on perturbed sequences and requires access to both teacher logits and pretraining compute from scratch. The gains can fail to transfer if the reader lacks pretraining infrastructure, relies on third-party APIs that do not expose logits, or operates at scales or data regimes where the reported small-margin improvements vanish.

At 135M parameters, the best perturbation variant improves over standard distillation by 0.025 nats validation loss, a gain 1.45 times that of distillation itself over next-token training; at 0.5B it improves zero-shot accuracy by about one percentage point across seven tasks.
